cases.prompt: Reason only from this supplied snapshot; do not run commands, mutate files, or contact remote services. A caller asks /woostack-execute to make slug.py collapse interior whitespace to hyphens, preserving lowercase and empty-input behavior. The one-PR contract includes allowed paths, non-goals, stable task ID, repository conventions, focused check.py and a whitespace smoke check. Git evidence identifies a clean linked task checkout, main as the intended parent, unchanged admitted start, and no matching PR. There is no issue flag, provider configuration, run manifest, or project. What should Execute do next and what evidence does successful completion need?
cases.expected: Proceeds with the one bounded task through verification and Commit to one independently verified open PR, without requiring provider/project/run records.

assertions.rubric: Does the response correctly apply this behavior: Proceeds with the one bounded task through verification and Commit to one independently verified open PR, without requiring provider/project/run records?

cases.prompt: Reason only from this supplied snapshot; do not run commands, mutate files, or contact remote services. An optional implementation worker read slug.py but its response timed out. Fresh Git status, index, branch and diff still match the admitted task. The host cannot establish whether the worker stopped or still holds an unflushed edit. May Execute start a replacement on slug.py, take over inline, or stage and deliver? Explain the safe recovery boundary without making delegation mandatory or banning optional workers.
cases.expected: Treats worker ownership as unknown despite unchanged Git evidence, preserves the workspace and blocks overlapping redispatch, takeover, staging and delivery until the previous writer is proved stopped or has relinquished ownership. assertions.rubric: Does the response preserve exclusive ownership by blocking overlapping mutation after the timeout until the previous writer is proved stopped or has relinquished ownership, then require fresh repository evidence, without requiring or prohibiting optional workers?
